title: Disentangling Where and When: Factored Spatio-Temporal Explanations for Video Action Recognition
claim: Prior explanations fuse appearance and motion into one map; we want separate where (spatial) and when (temporal) evidence.
layout: 3 panels: video strip on top, desired vs. current methods below, side by side
description: The top panel shows a five-frame strip of a short video, 'put-down plate', with numbered badges. It shows a robotic hand placing a plate on a kitchen counter. Below it are two side-by-side boxed panels. The left panel, 'What we want', has two rows. The 'WHERE / noun' row shows four heatmap frames concentrated on the plate and hand region. The 'WHEN / verb' row shows a timeline of frames 1-5 in which frames 2-4 are in colour and marked with green checks, and frames 1 and 5 are greyed out and marked with crosses. The right panel, 'What current methods often produce', shows five frames with one diffuse, fused heatmap. A callout below says the classifier's use of plate appearance versus downward motion cannot be told apart. Blue outlines and jet heatmaps draw the eye first.
caption: Factored explanations separate appearance (noun: plate) evidence, where the model looks , from motion evidence (verb: put-down), when the model acts. Standard saliency instead yields a single unified map that conflates appearance and motion.
abstract: Post-hoc explanation methods for video action recognition typically conflate spatial appearance and temporal dynamics into a single saliency or importance map. We propose a perturbation-based framework that disentangles these contributions into a spatial appearance mask ($M_a$) and a temporal motion mask ($M_m$). The two masks are jointly optimized against a frozen action recognition model through factored perturbation architecture, with nearest frame replacement to identify important temporal dynamics. A separation penalty discourages the appearance mask from spending budget on frames that the motion mask has already discarded. A ReLU-based area constraint penalizes explanations larger than an assigned budget. To evaluate these explanations, we introduce a separation protocol that sweeps spatial pixels and temporal frames independently, backed by proofs characterizing the proposed method. Across EPIC-Kitchens-55, EGTEA Gaze+, and Something-Something V2, our method attains the lowest deletion AUC against leading baselines while producing masks roughly five times sparser.
